venue.name: Douglas Walker Sculpture Studio
venue.description: Douglas Walker Sculpture Studio is the working studio and garden gallery of the sculptor Douglas Walker, on the North Island Highway at Black Creek in the Comox Valley. He makes kinetic wind sculptures, fountains and water features from brass, copper, glass and recycled musical instruments, and his current work is shown in the garden around the home he shares with Jann Hall. The site says visitors are welcome year round, either by appointment or as a drop in. Everything published here is about buying or commissioning a sculpture. There are no tours, workshops, prices, opening hours or anything else written for a children's group, so no program is recorded.
venue.address: 8138 Island Highway, Black Creek, BC V9J 1H1
venue.hours_notes: No opening hours are published. The site says visitors are welcome year round and that you can call ahead for an appointment or just drop by.

gaps: No program has been recorded. The site says on its contact page that visitors are welcome year round and can call ahead or drop by, but it never mentions groups, schools, daycares, children or classes anywhere. Nothing is bookable by a group leader, so no Group visit was invented.
Whether a children's group can come at all is unanswered. The site is silent rather than refusing, so this is worth one phone call before it is ruled in or out.
Price: nothing is published about the cost of visiting. The site's prices are all for buying sculpture.
Youngest age welcomed: not stated. This is a private home and garden with metal sculpture and standing water, and the site says nothing about how it works with small children.

Group size, notice needed to book, lunch space, washrooms, wet weather cover, parking, and whether the paths are pushchair or wheelchair friendly are all unstated. It is a residential acreage, so parking a bus is a real question to ask.
Opening hours are not published at all, only the year round welcome and the offer of an appointment.
Coordinates were geocoded from the street address on the contact page. The page's map is a plain address search embed with no place pin in it.

Images: the site publishes no photograph of the driveway, the entrance, the studio building or of any visitor. The six home page slides are all photographs of individual sculptures, two of which are recorded here because they at least show the garden setting. Both alt lines are the site's own words.
The site's newest dated content is from 2017 and the footer reads 2015, so some of it may be old. The pages themselves load and the contact details are presented as current.
